'''Etirha''', officially The '''United Provinces of Etirha''' is a country in [[Atirha]]. It's [[Etirhan provinces|seven provinces]] and 1 [[Moaneill|territory]] extend from the [[Uscea Sea]] to the [[Rianian Ocean]], making it the world's [[List of countries and dependencies by area|nineteenth-largest country]] by total area. It borders [[Pelan]], [[Gaeiya]], [[Laselteh]] and [[Grazail]] to the north and [[Disal Nila]] to the South. The territory of [[Moaneill]], located in [[New Ayre]], borders [[Aplasia]] to the north, [[Maalle]] and [[Nia]] to the west, and [[Veelmit]] to the south. The country is characterised by a wide range of both meteorological and [[wikipedia:Geology|geological regions]]. With a [[List of countries and dependencies by population|population of over 74 million]], it has widely varying [[List of countries and dependencies by population density|population densities]], with the majority residing in urban areas and other areas of the country being sparsely populated. Etirha's capital is [[Albiran]], and its three largest metropolitan areas (excluding [[Albiran]]) are [[Lunru]], [[Dazmir]], and [[Veshtar]].

The continent of [[Atirha]] was first [[Discovery of Atirha|discovered]] by [[Taval|Tavalan]] traders in 1240, and the earliest known settlement was located in what is now [[Peka]]. Beginning in the 16th century, the [[Taval|Tavalan]] and [[Merela Sta|Merelan]] expeditions explored and later settled along the eastern coast. As a consequence of various armed conflicts, [[Redea Kingdom|Redea]] (modern-day [[Siana]]) ceded its colony of [[Ternjmeia]] in the [[Redea succession war]]. In 1617, four of the six colonies were unified under a [[wikipedia:Federation#Federagovernments|federal government]] in [[Albiran]] into the United Provinces. Etirha was formed as a [[federal dominion]] of four provinces. This began an accretion of provinces and territories, resulting in the displacement of other colonial populations and a process of [[Etirha-Merela Sta relations|decreasing relations]] with its overlord [[Merela Sta]]. This coalesced into the [[Etirhan Independence War|Etirhan independence war]] in 1641, highlighted by the demand for the disbanding of the provinces, and culminated in the ''[[Etirha Act]] 1650'', which granted the province independence from the crown in [[Ayuma]].

Etirha is a [[wikipedia:Semi-presidential_republic|semi-presidential republic]] and a [[wikipedia:Federation|federal state]]. The country's head of government is the [[High Minister]] who holds office by their ability to command the confidence of the elected lower house ([[Etirhan National Assembly|National Assembly]]) and is appointed by the upper house ([[State Council|State Council)]]. It is very highly ranked in international measurements of [[wikipedia:Open_government|government transparency]], [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|quality of life]], economic competitiveness, innovation, [[wikipedia:Education|ducation]] and human rights. It is one of the world's most ethnically diverse and [[wikipedia:Multiculturalism|multicultural]] nations, the product of large-scale [[wikipedia:Immigration|immigration]]. Etirha’s long and complex relationship with the other major power in [[Atirha]], [[Raledria]], has had a significant impact on its history, economy, and culture.

A developed country, Etirha has a high [[List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita|nominal per capita income]] globally, and its [[wikipedia:Developed_country|advanced economy]] ranks among the largest in the world [[List of countries by GDP (nominal)|by nominal GDP]], relying chiefly upon its abundant natural resources and well-developed [[wikipedia:International_trade|international trade]] networks. Recognised as a major power, Etirha's support for multilateralism and [[wikipedia:nternationalism|internationalism]] has been closely related to its foreign relations policies of [[wikipedia:Peacekeeping|peacekeeping]] and aid for developing countries. Etirha promotes its domestically shared values through participation in multiple [[Etirhan International organisations|international organisations]] and forums.
